techStack: React 19, TypeScript 5.7, Vite 6, Vitest 3 (not Jest) — test config lives inside vite.config.ts
useDebounce<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T — generic hook; delay is a plain number parameter, no built-in conditional logic
noUnusedLocals / noUnusedParameters enforced in tsconfig.app.json — the fix must not introduce unused variables
No external debounce utility; the hand-rolled hook is the only debounce mechanism
Passing a computed expression (ternary) as delayMs is idiomatic — the hook's useEffect depends on [value, delayMs], so a delay change re-runs the effect automatically
No named-constant pattern for numeric literals in this codebase — inline literals 0 and 300 are consistent with project style
features: FilterContext.tsx exports FilterProvider and useFilterContext; their public interface (FilterContextValue type and exported symbols) must remain unchanged
Current bug site: line 51 — `const debouncedSearch = useDebounce(search, 0);` hardcodes 0 ms, defeating the debounce
useFilteredProducts.ts consumes debouncedSearch (not search) from context — must NOT be modified
Category, inStockOnly, and sortBy filters are not routed through useDebounce and must stay immediate (no debounce)
saveCurrentFilters snapshots the raw `search` value (not debouncedSearch) — must remain unchanged
Tests that must pass: debounceSearch.test.tsx, filtering.test.tsx, clearFilters.test.tsx, sorting.test.tsx, pagination.test.tsx, app.render.test.tsx, loadingError.test.tsx
architecture: Layer structure: src/api → src/context (FilterContext) → src/hooks (useDebounce, useFilteredProducts) → src/components → src/pages
FilterContext owns all filter state and computes debouncedSearch; components read via useFilterContext()
Fix is a single-file, single-line change — no other files need touching
useDebounce hook is already correct and must not be modified; the fix lives entirely at the call site
edgeCases: Initial render (search === ''): delay resolves to 0, debouncedSearch initialises to '' synchronously — no regression
Rapid typing (keystrokes < 300 ms apart): each keystroke cancels the previous 300 ms timer and schedules a new one; only the final value fires — correct standard debounce behaviour

Clear after partial typing: search goes from non-empty to ''; delayMs switches 300→0; useEffect cleanup cancels the pending 300 ms timer before scheduling a 0 ms one — debouncedSearch becomes '' immediately with no stale-filter flash
clearFilters() path: sets search to '' via setSearchState(''), same zero-delay path as manual clear — clearFilters.test.tsx asserts 'Showing 15 products' immediately

Category active during clear: category state is independent of debouncedSearch; clearing search (zero delay) leaves category untouched — 'clearing search while a category is active' test expects 5 products
TypeScript generics: T inferred as string at the call site; both ternary branches are number — call signature fully satisfied, no type error
Unmount with pending timer: useDebounce already returns () => clearTimeout(timer) in effect cleanup; the fix does not change this — no memory leak or stale-state warning
delayMs in effect dependency array: a delay change from 300 to 0 re-triggers the effect even if value is already ''; this guarantees the zero-delay timer is scheduled on clear, not residual 300 ms

tasks.requirement: Requirement 1: The useDebounce call in FilterContext.tsx passes a delay of 300 when search is non-empty and 0 when search is '' — e.g. useDebounce(search, search === '' ? 0 : 300) or equivalent.
tasks.description: In FilterContext.tsx line 51, change `useDebounce(search, 0)` to `useDebounce(search, search === '' ? 0 : 300)`. This single-line change satisfies requirements 1–5 (300 ms debounce for typing, immediate clear, stale-timer cancellation on clear, no memory leak) while leaving the hook, the public interface, useFilteredProducts, and all other filter state untouched (requirements 6–10).
